Basically there are three scenarios:

  1. In the first scenario, there is a button that instantly kills all the humans humans in the world when pressed. Every hour, a random monkey is sent into this room and for an hour, they have a chance to press that button. After that, a monkey will be sent out and replaced with a new one. The monkeys do not know what the button does. Do you expect that a eventually there will be a monkey who accidentally or purposefully presses the button?

  2. In the second scenario, there is a button that instantly kills all the humans in the world when pressed. Every hour, a random person is sent into the room. They are informed that all the humans (including the one who presses the button) will die when the button is pressed. Some believe it, others don't. A few even know that it really does kill the humans. After an hour, a human will be sent out and a new human is called in. Do you expect that a eventually there will be a human who accidentally or purposefully presses the button?

  3. In the third scenario, there is a button that also instantly kills all the humans in the world when pressed. Every hour, a random robot with superintelligent AI is sent into the room. You don't know what the goals of superintelligent AI are, you don't know what measures it could take to achieve them and you don't know its exact intelligence (apart from that you only know that it's much, much smarter than humans). What you know is that the AI knows exactly what the button does. After an hour, a robot will be sent out and a new robot with new superintelligent AI is sent in. Do you expect that a eventually there will be a robot with superintelligent AI who presses the button?

If you answered "Yes" to all three scenarios, then do really you think it's the intelligence that's the main problem?

Also, in which scenario, the button is likely to be pressed first?
How would you respond to "3 human killing buttons scenarios" thought experiment?

I'd press the button just to see what would actually happen. It's a no-lose scenario. Pressing the button would either satisfy my curiosity, or kill me. And in the later case I'd be too dead to mourn humanity or feel regret.

Yes to the first two and no to the third.
The monkey will likely press the button first out of sheer curiosity. Natural animal extinct. Explore your environment. Monkeys are naturally curious and would have no sense of ethical restraint for obvious reasons.
The humans will take some time depending on who is in the room. Someone malicious enough will eventually press that button be it for religious reasons or to eradicate humanity for its transgressions (think global warming fundamentalist) or someone mentally retarded and incapable of understanding the warning falls to the monkey scenario.
With the third option it's hard to tell because the nature of AI is not yet realized. It would entirely depend on how its programming was developed. Emergent AI (although this seems to be less likely ATM) would be much more likely to press the button given enough iterations as theoretically their intelligence would be much more random. Traditional AIs would likely have programming restraints to prevents such an action from taking place similar to three laws safe.

I think intelligence is key to this scenario but so are reward schemes. If the monkeys were intelligent enough they would intentionally press that button as it would greatly benefit their species.
With humans intelligence and nobility (for lack of a better word) are not cleanly linked. There are plenty of very intelligent people in prison for terrible crimes. So long as the person had enough intelligence to fully understand the potential for their actions reward scheme behavior would come into effect (this can be modeled as a game theory problem). All it would take is for someone who actively wishes the end of mankind (those people do exist although they are rather rare) or someone uninhibited enough to test the game.
With the AI it would depend a lot on the nature of human AI relations, fundamental programming, and the degree to which the AI exhibits personality. It's hard to speculate without knowing more.
